newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares take tumble in jittery trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares take tumble in jittery trade.

text.p: German shares took a tumble on Friday as continued fears of interest rate hikes made it impossible for the market to break its recent downbeat trend.
The 30-share DAX index fell nearly two percent in a bourse session characterised by low volumes and high volatility, ending down 78.57 points at 4,188.28 points.

A sharp slide on the Dow Jones index put further pressure on prices in the after-bourse electronic session, sending the index tumbling through a psychological support at 4,100 points. The IBIS DAX closed down 117.94 points at 4,077.59.
"A lot of people are running for cover out there. Volumes are thin but the momentum is strong," a Frankfurt dealer said.
The dollar fell against the mark amid escalating expectations for a German rate hike soon, adding to pressure on the German equity market.

Among the most resistant shares of the day was utility RWE AG, the outperformer on Thursday after it announced plans to shelve an unpopular system of multiple voting rights attached to shares held mainly by local municipalities.
The move was viewed as opening up the company to international investors, by loosening old ties on its equity.
RWE common stock rose strongly in early bourse, but fell back to end the day down 30 pfennigs at 86.70 marks, still more stable than the broader market.
The Assumption holiday in the southern states of Germany also contibuted to keeping volumes low.
